- How zeroization/crypto-shredding is handled on decommission
- TLS mTLS support and automated cert rotation options (ACME or enterprise CA integrations)
- Any required customer actions for Dedicated/Private deployments vs Hosted

Alice — thanks for the clear list. I’m attaching a short handover packet and a diagram that answers most of these at a glance. Key bullets up front:

• BYOK/HSM import model: we support client-side wrapped key import (PKCS#7/PKCS#11 compatible) into FIPS 140-certified HSM appliances. For Hosted we use customer-wrapped import with remote attestation; for Dedicated/Private we can arrange direct HSM import or on-prem key transfer depending on your policy.

• Export policy: Redwood does not provide plaintext export of private key material from an HSM. We support wrapped export (customer-held wrapping keys) under tight change-control and approved SOPs — export is logged and requires signed approval.

• Rotation: recommended KEK rotation every 12 months for standard workloads, data-key rotation can be customized; emergency rotation window is typically <4 hours with pre-warmed keys for high-throughput routes. See attached kek_rotation_schedule.xlsx.

• Zeroization: HSM zeroize is an irreversible hardware operation; we perform zeroize on decommission, log the operation, and provide an audit record (serial, timestamp, operator id). For Private deployments you control the zeroize policy; for Hosted we coordinate per your SLA.

• TLS / PKI binding: we support mutual TLS, per-tenant mTLS with client cert validation and per-route TLS profiles. Automated rotation: integration with ACME or your enterprise CA (SCEP/EST) is supported; we offer a connector that can renew certs and roll them with zero-downtime swap. See tls_binding_diagram.png.

• Evidence: we can provide HSM attestation (manufacture-signed certs), FIPS cert copies, and a signed attestation statement. We also map controls to SOC 2 and can provide logs for key life-cycle events.

Next steps: Monica will coordinate a 60-minute working session with your security and infra leads to walk the handover checklist and confirm acceptance criteria. Proposed slots: Wed 12/2 10:00 or Thu 12/3 14:00 PT. Which works best?

Irene

Hi Alice — quick answers to your three points below; happy to expand in the workshop.

> 1) "Wrapped export" controls and vendor interoperability
We only allow key material to leave an HSM under a customer-approved wrapping key. Exports are possible in a wrapped form but require a multi-party approval (ticket, signed approval from your procurement/security alias, and an internal operator). Wrapped keys adhere to standard formats (RFC 7517/JWK, PKCS#8 when applicable) and can be re-imported into compatible HSMs that support the same wrapping algorithms (RSA-OAEP or AES-KW). Cross-vendor re-import depends on algorithm support and vendor key-format support; our onboarding engineers validate compatibility during the handover.

> 2) Zeroization witness and tamper evidence
All hardware HSMs we deploy for customer workloads are tamper-evident and come with vendor seal IDs. For Dedicated/Private we provide physical manifests and serial numbers plus photographs of seals and signed attestation from the vendor at delivery. Zeroization is performed via the HSM vendor tooling and is observable in the audit stream; we capture the zeroize event (operator id, timestamp, HSM serial) and deliver a signed event record. For higher assurance requirements we support a third-party witness process (mutually agreed vendor / auditor) and escrowed audit artifacts.

> 3) Customer-managed keys and transit guarantees
Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we support keys that are generated and wrapped by the customer and never persisted in plaintext within Redwood systems. For Hosted we offer a BYOK flow where the customer retains the wrapping key; Redwood never has access to the unwrapped key material. In all cases service operations that require key use (e.g., wrap/unwrap) happen inside the HSM boundary and are logged.

Attachments above include the rotation schedule and the handover checklist which shows the acceptance gates we use for onboarding. I'll add a short attestation template (PDF) before the call so procurement has a document for signatures.
